messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 17:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (context-length profiling & pricing)

Thanks again for taking the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

Summary of needs (from today's call)
- High-throughput customer-facing assistant for support + intelligent search.
- Mixed context-length profile: most queries short, but ~10% require longer context (32k) and a small slice (~1%) will need very long context (128k) for deep historical transcripts.
- Target production launch: Q1 2027 pilot, then scale.

Action items we agreed on
1) ACME to share sample usage profile (avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, % of queries per context tier) — we can use that to build pricing band and estimate monthly token volume.
2) Redwood to return a preliminary unit-economics estimate ($/1M tokens) and recommended model/quantization profile for 8k/32k/128k contexts.
3) Schedule follow-up pricing review once we have the sample export (2-week target).

Attached: context_profile.csv (example format) — if you can send an export of a representative day/week, that will let us compute realistic monthly token volume and show different cost scenarios.

A couple of clarifying Qs that will help pricing accuracy:
- Do you have a target budget (ballpark $/1M tokens) or a preferred unit cost to work toward?
- Any hard latency SLOs for the assistant (p50/p95)?

Next steps: please reply with the sample export and the budget target if you have one. I'll draft a short pricing memo with 3 tiers (pilot, steady-state, optimized-quantized) once we have numbers.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0124

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (context-length profiling & pricing)

Tom — this is perfect, thanks for the numbers and the export. Quick back-of-envelope math and follow-ups so we can be concrete in the pricing memo: 

Back-of-envelope token math (using your averages)
- tokens per request = avg prompt (120) + avg completion (450) = 570 tokens/request
- estimated monthly tokens = 25,000,000 requests * 570 = 14,250,000,000 tokens/month (14.25B)

Implications for unit economics
- At your target of $800 / 1M tokens, monthly cost = (14,250M tokens / 1M) * $800 = $11,400,000 / month (uncommitted, pay-as-you-go).
- There are typical levers to reduce that: reserved capacity discounts, model-variant routing (route short queries to cheaper small/quantized models), KV/prefix caching for repeated context, and batching for throughput.

Questions to refine the estimate
- Are you expecting steady 25M requests every month or is there seasonality/spikes (e.g., 2x peak days)?
- For the 10% 32k and 1% 128k slices, do those requests tend to come with longer completions (higher than the 450 avg) or are they mostly longer prompts? The token split matters for pricing bands.

What I'll send next (by end of day tomorrow):
- Preliminary pricing memo with three lines: 8k band, 32k band, 128k band (with reserved vs. on-demand examples), and a couple of options that hit your $800 target via commit tiers.
- A short multi-month cost projection (pilot -> steady-state) and recommended rollout (pilot with 8k/32k mix, then enable 128k fallbacks).

Would you prefer a single 30-min call to run through the memo or a written note + follow-up only if you want to discuss?

Thanks,
Marissa

Attachments referenced: pricing_model_v2.xlsx (estimates & scenario sheet)

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@acme.com>

- The 32k and 128k requests are primarily longer prompts (verbatim transcripts + user history) and often have longer completions (~600-900 tokens) when they include generated summaries.
